newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania leu steady, market awaiting c.bank moves.
newsitem.headline: Romania leu steady, market awaiting c.bank moves.

text.p: Romania's leu currency closed flat on Wednesday at 5,950/980 to the dollar in an interbank market reflecting a hard currency squeeze.
Traders were bracing for central bank (BNR) moves at the weekly refinancing auction on Thursday, when they expect the BNR to drain further leu liquidity from the money market.
"Such a move will provide support to the leu which might stabilise somewhere between 6,000 to 6,200 to the dollar," said a trader with one of the four market-making dealer banks.
Cross quotes of other currencies continued to offer a leu-dollar price of 6,500 but some traders suggested that in the coming days those rates would rebound towards 6,000.
"We might get back to normal trading and we might not use other currencies as a back door for better prices," said one.

Local traders have used cross trading in other currencies since last March, when the market was restricted to four dealer banks by the former leftist government to keep the leu overvalued against the dollar ahead of elections.
Operators said the market was poised for details about the reform package which Romania's new ruling centrist coalition is negotiating with the International Monetary Fund.

Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea will hold a news confrence late on Thursday to give the first details of the reform pledges made in exchange for renewed funds from the IMF, which suspended credits to Romania last year.
Leu-dollar retail rates stayed at about 6,000/200.
Short-term rates drifted higher to 67 percent from 65 in early trading on a money market short of leu funds.
